{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately BEFORE the current text in the same invented story.","text":"By February, Mara had learned to recognize the office printer’s warning noises. A faint click meant the paper tray was nearly empty; a grinding shudder meant somebody had fed it a form with a bent corner. She knew which cupboard held the spare toner and how to coax the jammed drawer open without snapping its latch.

Nobody had asked her to learn these things. They simply needed doing, and Mara was usually the first to notice. When the weekly figures arrived with a column shifted out of place, she corrected the formula. When a new hire couldn’t follow the instructions for booking a room, she rewrote them on a sticky note and left it beside the calendar.

“You’re a lifesaver,” her manager said, already turning toward the next meeting.

Mara smiled because it was easier than explaining that she didn’t want to save anyone. She wanted the work to make sense. She wanted to spend a day solving problems that stayed solved, instead of patching the same leaks while everyone hurried past the bucket.

After work, she stopped at a stationery shop and bought a narrow notebook with a blue cloth cover. She told herself it was for keeping track of appointments. At home, she wrote down the date and the grocery items she’d forgotten to buy. Then she sat at the kitchen table, listening to rain tick against the window, and left the pen poised above the next blank line.

For a long time, she couldn’t think of anything worth writing. Finally, she turned to a fresh page and began with a small heading: Things I might do someday. She underlined someday once, lightly, as if it were a word that might startle and run."}
